rationale: The Latin anchor *extorquere* (to wrest/extort, i.e. compel by pressure) strongly points to the sense of compelling someone to act through pressure or necessity, which aligns with coerce.v.01. While *repellere* (to drive back/repel) adds a physical thrust, the combined sense of the two Latin glosses — compelling or wresting something from someone — best matches the coercive pressure sense of coerce.v.01 rather than purely physical movement.
